data.text:
Asia is reeling from the combined impact of deadly cyclones and relentless monsoon rains, with the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) describing the disaster as "like a tsunami" in terms of its destructive scale.

Worst-hit nations and WMO's assessment

Clare Nullis, WMO spokesperson, told reporters in Geneva that Indonesia, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Vietnam are among the countries hardest hit. She attributed the catastrophe to "a combination of monsoon-related rainfall and tropical cyclone activity" – a deadly mix that has triggered widespread chaos.

Nullis highlighted the rarity of tropical cyclone Senyar, which last week battered northern Sumatra (Indonesia), peninsular Malaysia and southern Thailand. The storm unleashed "torrential rainfall, widespread flooding and landslides" – an event she stressed is highly unusual so close to the Equator.

"It's not something that we see very often, and it means the impacts are magnified because local communities have got no experience in this," she explained. She also noted that flooding consistently tops the list of climate hazards in Asia, citing WMO's annual State Of The Climate reports, and emphasized: "Asia is very, very vulnerable to floods."

Devastating toll across regions

Indonesia: Quoting data from the Indonesian National Disaster Office, as of Tuesday, Nullis said the country has recorded 604 fatalities, 464 missing people and 2,600 injuries. Around 1.5 million people have been affected, with over 570,000 displaced from their homes.

Vietnam: The Southeast Asian nation has been "battered for weeks" and is now "bracing for yet more heavy rainfall," Nullis revealed. Exceptional rains in recent weeks have flooded historic sites and popular tourist resorts, causing massive damage. In late October, a meteorological station in central Vietnam logged a national 24-hour rainfall record of 1,739 millimetres – a figure Nullis called "really enormous." She added it is "the second-highest known total anywhere in the world for 24-hour rainfall" and noted the WMO's Extremes Evaluation Committee is formally assessing the data. A reading above 1,700 mm would set a new record for both the Northern Hemisphere and Asia.

Sri Lanka: Cyclone Ditwah made landfall on the country's east coast last week, turning the situation into a "fast-moving humanitarian emergency," according to Ricardo Pires, spokesperson for the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF). The cyclone has affected around 1.4 million people, including 275,000 children. Pires warned that "with communications down and roads blocked, the true number of children impacted is likely even higher." Homes have been swept away, entire communities cut off and essential services for children – such as clean water, healthcare and schooling – severely disrupted. He also noted that displacement has forced families into unsafe, overcrowded shelters, while flooding and damaged water systems are raising the risk of disease outbreaks. "The needs far outweigh the available resources right now," Pires said, appealing for more humanitarian funding to support vulnerable groups.

UN's response and condolences

UN Secretary-General António Guterres has expressed deep sadness over the loss of life across the region. In a statement released by his spokesperson, he extended condolences to the families of the victims and reaffirmed solidarity with all those affected.

The UN has also pledged to support relief efforts, with officials stating: "The United Nations is in close contact with authorities in all four countries and stands ready to support relief and response efforts. UN Country Teams remain at the disposal of governments to provide necessary assistance."

Climate change link

Nullis linked the intensity of the devastating weather to climate change, explaining that rising global temperatures "increase the potential risk of more extreme rainfall because a warmer atmosphere holds more moisture."

"That's the law of physics," she concluded. "We are seeing more extreme rainfall, and we will continue to do so in the future."

■ TESLA $TSLA ($446.74, +4.08%):

- Giga Shanghai posted that they do not have dedicated storage space for parts and retrieve parts directly from containers and load them onto the production line. "We achieve exceptional efficiency from supply chain to production line. The localization rate of parts at Giga Shanghai exceeds 95%, and on average, a complete vehicle rolls off the production line every 30 seconds."

- The Electric Vehicle Council conducted month-long road tests of FSD capability in Brisbane and Melbourne using a Model Y as part of an Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA)-funded strata-charging project in partnership with NOX Energy. The vehicle successfully completed site assessments for multi-unit residential charging infrastructure while demonstrating strong performance as a corporate fleet option, offering comfort, safety, and versatility across urban environments with capacity for the entire team. The Council highlighted Tesla's rollout of FSD in Australia as a significant step forward for clean, connected, and autonomous transport.

- Joe Tegtmeyer (@JoeTegtmeyer) reported that construction at Cortex 2 in Giga Texas has progressed to installing chiller plant piers, platforms, and conduit. A suspected water tank enclosure may be on the east side. And Robotic Avenue is being extended. Follow/subscribe to Joe and support his work!

- Robotaxi validation testing spotted on Interstate 95 North, just south of Portland, Maine. Pic by reddit u/GRADIUSIC_CYBER.

- Andrea Stroppa (@andst7) reported that Tesla hosted Rome Mayor Roberto Gualtieri and Mobility Assessor Eugenio Patanè for a demonstration of FSD in Rome. This marked the first time an Italian mayor personally tested the system. The drive navigated typical Roman traffic challenges including complex intersections, roundabouts, pedestrian crossings, and mixed traffic with cars, bicycles, and scooters. Assessor Patanè stated Rome’s administration is open to pragmatically evaluating innovations that enhance road safety and mobility quality while respecting existing rules and driver responsibility.

- Tesla Thailand is at the Motor Expo 2025 in Bangkok, Thailand, at IMPACT Muang Thong Thani, Challenger Hall 2, Booth B09 until December 10th 25. The display highlights Optimus, Supercharger Network, and explains why the Model Y and 3 remain the world’s best-selling EVs.

■ SPACEX:

- Yesterday evening, gorgeous launch 160 of Falcon 9 Starlink 6-95 took place from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida. B1077 This was the 25th flight for first stage booster B1077. It previously launched Crew-5, GPS III Space Vehicle 06, Inmarsat I6-52, CRS-28, Intelsat G-37, NG-20, TD7, and 17 Starlink missions. The booster landed on a drone ship A Shortfall of Gravitas in the Atlantic Ocean. 29 Starlinks were deployed.

- SpaceX posted Raptor 3 Validation testing of a Starship V3 ascent burn. The test focused on the engine's performance under conditions experienced by Starship's three central inner engines during the initial ascent phase to space. As stated, multiple iterations of this test will replicate varying environmental factors, such as thrust levels, thermal loads, and pressure profiles encountered by these engines, which operate continuously from liftoff through main engine cutoff.

- There was an odd removal of the left chopstick actuator at Pad 2.

■ NEURALINK:

- DJ Seo (@djseo), Neuralink's Co-Founder, President, and COO, delivered a presentation at multiple schools outlining the company's history since 2016, including early Tesla integrations and brain-machine interface advancements. He details the next-generation surgical robot's upgrades; covers robot components like insertion arms, cameras, and grippers; and enhanced neural signal recording with reduced noise and improved bandwidth. Highlights include:

- Over 10,000 people are on the PRIME Study wait list.

- New HQ is being built in Austin. Not sure if this is the location at 2200 Caldwell Lane in Del Valle.

- The next-gen surgical robot will insert threads into the brain in 1.5 seconds, achieving compatibility with 99% of the global human population.

- The needle will extend to depths exceeding 50mm from the brain's surface, enabling access to additional areas.

- The needle cartridge production costs 95% less than the prior version.

- Electrode arrays have 1,024 channels at 10-micron sites.

Per DJ, "We’ve made great progress so far and are working hard to end the year with 20 participants. But this is just the beginning. We still have a long way to go..."

■ STARLINK:

- SpaceX will launch Starlink in South Korea starting tomorrow, December 4th, with a residential plan providing unlimited data for 87,000 KRW/mo. ($59/mo.) and kit costs of 550,000 KRW ($375). This will include a 30-day free trial for new subscribers. Sales occur through resellers SK Telink and KT Sat.

- The Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia (CRAN) has invited public and stakeholder feedback on Starlink’s telecommunications and spectrum license applications, with submissions due by December 12th. CRAN Executive for Communication and Consumer Relations Mufaro Nesongano explained that the review process evaluates the application under Section 39 of the Communications Act, covering ministerial-approved ownership, technical and financial capabilities, service neutrality, standards compliance, and national security.

- The Emirates' new Starlink-powered 777-300ER (A6-EPF) at the Dubai Airshow. The onboard connection delivered fast, stable, and responsive performance with consistent coverage enabled by six new access points throughout the cabin.

- Data Lake Inc. collaborated with Melco Resorts Foundation and the Philippines Department of Education to deliver Starlink High-Performance kits, gigabit routers, Omada access points, and structured cabling to 100 remote public schools across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. The project enables virtual classes, access to DepEd resources, online meetings, and digital assessments. This has positioned schools as community digital hubs for parent communication, LGU coordination, and disaster response.
